Most suitability for this technology lies in the western edge of the state, which comes from its proximity to the Green River. The largest interruption in the suitability of this region is due to a series of wilderness areas, wildlife refuges, and Dinosaur National Monument. Additional restrictions come into play with the slope constraint, as Moffat County has an array of mountains and canyons occupying its western, southern, and eastern edges. When the water requirement is relaxed (though not eliminated) for the SMR siting regime shown in Table C.M2, we see a significant portion of the south edge of Moffat County open up for potential development. This is due to the proximity of Moffat County to the White River, which flows through and gives its name to Rio Blanco County to the south of Moffat. In Table C.M3, there is a much larger swath of viable land in the north of Moffat that is not impacted by the same slope restrictions as the rest of the county. With the northern and eastern ends of the county opened up, the impact of other criteria on suitability are more apparent. In particular, a sizeable region in the southeast is shown to be prone to landslides, though the overall impact of the restriction is minimal.
